records.text: Clump: a bulky mass of human-like limbs adapted to cramped spaces such as vents, pipes, cabinets and narrow recesses. It commonly hunts from concealment, remaining still until prey comes close, then rapidly extending one or more long arms to seize, immobilize and drag the victim toward its central mass or into the confined space where it is hiding. When forced to move it can be unexpectedly fast and can use its many limbs to climb or traverse vents. External references agree on the limb-cluster appearance, close-range ambush/grab tactic and confined-space preference, but disagree on exact reach and speed, so no hard numeric range is canon here. Project hard lock applies: a Clump is never friendly or neutral toward humans.

records.text: Duller: a tall, elongated dark-gray humanoid with long arms, an unnatural or frail-looking frame and no normal human facial features. External references agree that it can no-clip part of its body through solid walls, especially an arm, to seize prey on the opposite side and drag the victim away; despite its thin appearance it can move quickly and exert substantial strength. External sources conflict on overt behavior: one describes direct avoidance outside its wall-ambush tactic while another describes active stalking and hostility. Project canon therefore resolves only the gameplay boundary, not the disputed behavior: a Duller is never friendly or neutral toward humans, and apparent withdrawal must not be treated as safety. Hallucination/gas abilities, exact body variants and exact reach remain uncommitted because they are not consistently corroborated across the checked sources.

records.text: Hound visual/behavior supplement: externally corroborated descriptions depict a gaunt humanoid adapted to quadrupedal movement, with long dark hair around the head/back, elongated bony limbs, sharp claws and an oversized mouth lined with sharp teeth. It attacks by rushing and mauling at close range and has substantial striking/biting power despite its thin frame. The Wikidot account additionally reports that sustained direct eye contact can intimidate a Hound briefly, but this is a temporary reaction rather than neutrality or taming. Project canon remains authoritative for encounter behavior: Hounds are hostile predators, may hunt in groups, favor injured or isolated humans, pressure prey toward dead ends, can withdraw from strong resistance and return, and in Level 2 may coordinate through narrow corridors and deceptive footstep cues. External claims about eggs, transformation syndromes or bite-borne conversion vary by continuity and are not imported into game canon here.

records.text: False Puddle visual/behavior supplement: it camouflages as an ordinary flat Almond Water puddle while concealing a deep mouth or pit lined with sharp teeth beneath the liquid surface. External references consistently describe it as stationary: it does not chase prey, but waits on traversed ground for an unaware target to step into or interact with the apparent puddle, then snaps or closes around the victim and pulls/holds them down for consumption. Liquid Pain and sharp metal are repeatedly described as ways to force closure or injure the mouth lining, which agrees with current project canon; however, exact depth measurements differ among external versions and are not fixed here. Project canon also preserves the warning that apparent death can be feigned, so a closed or motionless False Puddle must not automatically be treated as neutralized. Alternate fan continuities that portray False Puddles as benevolent or harmless are incompatible with this game's entity hard lock and are excluded.

records.text: Wretch visual/behavior supplement: external Backrooms references consistently describe Wretches as distorted humanlike or zombie-like figures, commonly gaunt or skeletal-looking with exposed, reddish or otherwise visibly damaged flesh and severe bodily deformity. They are treated as dangerous close-range attackers that pursue or assault humans with brute force, and some continuities describe erratic vocalization, crude tool use or variable solitary/group behavior. Project canon remains authoritative where it is more specific: this game's Wretch moves irregularly, tolerates pain well, hunts through sound and scent, is commonly reported in lower Level 3 tunnels, and is never friendly or neutral toward humans. External material more strongly states that Wretches are former humans transformed by deprivation and a 'Wretched Cycle'; the repository only says they are believed or suspected to have once been human, so that stronger origin claim remains external-only and is not promoted to game canon. Exact mutation stages, transmission mechanics, cures, weapon use and numeric speed/strength are not imported.

records.text: Skin-Stealer visual/behavior supplement: external references commonly depict the undisguised entity as a tall pale-yellow or beige humanoid with sunken light-colored eyes and an abnormal flesh surface adapted to hold a victim's skin as a disguise. They can wear human skin and mimic speech; when attacking, external accounts describe overpowering isolated victims at close range with substantial physical strength. Project canon takes precedence over major continuity conflicts: in this game a Skin-Stealer can perform deep behavioral mimicry, retain enough copied memory to pass simple tests, live with a group for an extended period and damage the team before revealing itself; human appearance is therefore never proof of humanity, and ENTITY.GLOBAL_HARD_LOCK means it is never friendly or neutral toward humans. Wikidot-derived versions that describe non-hungry Skin-Stealers as docile and unable to understand language conflict with these repository locks, so those behavioral limits are explicitly rejected for runtime canon. External details such as transparent blood, a fixed disguise lifetime, precise hunger-state timing or exact anatomy remain uncommitted unless separately established in-repo.
